verdict.summary: You can build a public app for many independent merchants. Shopify must approve it before broad merchant installation. Community reports say review usually takes 5–10 business days, but it can take longer. If the app reads customer names, emails, addresses, or phone numbers, Shopify also requires a data-protection review.
verdict.activeEffort: 2–4 days, mostly building review-ready flows, disclosures, and test instructions
verdict.mainGate: A public app needs Shopify approval before broad merchant installation.

recommendation.text: Use public distribution for an app serving many independent merchants. Use an API-only app if your agent has no embedded Shopify interface. Use expiring offline tokens for background work.

sources.quote: Building for many merchants : You'll use public distribution.
Because they can't use ID tokens , they authenticate using the OAuth authorization code grant flow: redirect the merchant to Shopify, get their approval, and exchange a code for an access token.
Public apps must use expiring offline access tokens for GraphQL Admin API requests.

scopeTiers.text: Read product and stock data without customer data.

sources.quote: The most frequently used GraphQL Admin API scopes are read_products, read_orders, read_customers, read_inventory, read_draft_orders, read_discounts, read_content, and read_themes
0 No customer data No action required

scopeTiers.text: Read recent orders. This tier needs protected-data access when returned fields are customer data.

sources.quote: Orders are limited to the last 60 days. read_orders and write_orders cover that window.
1 Customer data excluding name, address, phone, and email fields Request access to protected customer data in the Partner Dashboard

scopeTiers.need: Summarize sales and recent order activity.

scopeTiers.text: Read customer contact details. This tier adds Shopify's data-protection review.

sources.quote: The most frequently used GraphQL Admin API scopes are read_products, read_orders, read_customers, read_inventory, read_draft_orders, read_discounts, read_content, and read_themes
2 Customer data including name, address, phone, or email fields Request access to protected customer data and fields in the Partner Dashboard
Participate in data protection reviews

scopeTiers.need: Personalize customer support or marketing work using names, emails, addresses, or phone numbers.

scopeTiers.text: Make catalog changes after merchant confirmation. A write scope already includes its matching read scope.

sources.quote: A write scope includes read.
write_products grants read_products, so declare the write scope on its own when your app needs both.
Ask for confirmation before writing data. Propose the change and show your UI so that the merchant can review it before anything is saved.

scopeTiers.need: Create or change products through agent-proposed actions.

essentials.text: Use expiring offline tokens for background GraphQL Admin API work. Access tokens last one hour. Refresh tokens start at 90 days and rotate on every refresh. Store both securely and serialize refreshes for each store.

sources.quote: Expiring offline access token 1 hour ( expires_in is 3600 )
Refresh token for an expiring offline access token 90 days ( refresh_token_expires_in is 7776000 ) when issued. Using it to refresh can shorten it.
Every refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token. Store both securely, and use the new refresh token in the next refresh request.
Don't do the two at the same time for the same store. Acquiring a token and refreshing one each retire the other's result

essentials.text: Add each callback URL in the Dev Dashboard or shopify.app.toml. The callback URL must match exactly.

sources.quote: Must exactly match a redirect URI you've configured in the Dev Dashboard or your app's configuration TOML file.
redirect_urls Yes array of string s matching a valid URL Users are redirected to these URLs as part of authorization code grant .

essentials.text: Use development stores instead of separate OAuth test users. An organization can have 250 development stores. These stores cannot process real transactions.

sources.quote: Organizations are limited to 250 dev stores.
Dev stores are for development and testing only. They can't be used in production or process real transactions.

essentials.text: Budget GraphQL requests per app and store. Standard stores get 100 points per second. Advanced stores get 200. Plus stores get 1,000. One query cannot exceed 1,000 points.

sources.quote: Standard 100 points/second
Advanced Shopify 200 points/second
Shopify Plus 1000 points/second
A single query may not exceed a cost of 1,000 points, regardless of plan limits.

essentials.text: App Store registration costs US$19 once per Partner account. Shopify keeps 0% of the first US$1 million in qualifying lifetime gross revenue. It keeps 15% above that. Billing also has a 2.9% processing fee and applicable sales tax.

sources.quote: you need to register with the Shopify App Store for a one-time fee of $19 USD per Partner account.
All billing is subject to a 2.9% processing fee and applicable sales tax. Fees and taxes are charged separately from revenue share.

essentials.text: Deploy production configuration with Shopify CLI. Public apps using old non-expiring offline tokens are blocked from new installs on January 1, 2027. Shopify rejects their GraphQL calls on April 1, 2027.

sources.quote: Instead, you can release your app configuration and extensions together with the deploy command.
Public apps that still use a non-expiring offline access token are delisted and blocked from new installs on January 1, 2027.
Starting April 1, 2027, Shopify rejects their GraphQL Admin API requests.

essentials.text: Run automated checks before submission. Configure app URLs, compliance webhooks, icon, and API contact details. Give an emergency email and phone number. Create a listing and choose its primary language.

sources.quote: These checks must be run and completed successfully to ensure functionality and reduce your app’s time spent in review.
The configuration section guides you to set up items such as URL(s) for your app, compliance webhooks, the app icon, and API contact details.
You need to provide an email and phone number in case critical technical issues with your app arise and we need to contact you.
Every app submission must specify a primary language and create at least one Shopify App Store listing.

essentials.text: Bind and verify OAuth state. Verify callback HMAC with a constant-time comparison. Verify webhook HMAC against the raw body. Keep the client secret only in server-side secret storage.

sources.quote: Compare the state parameter to the nonce you stored in step 1. If they don't match, reject the request.
Use a constant-time comparison, such as crypto.timingSafeEqual in Node.js or hmac.compare_digest in Python, so the check doesn't leak timing information.
HMAC verification requires the raw request body.
Never commit credentials to version control. Use environment variables or a secrets manager.

requests.text: Store RANDOM_STATE and verify it when Shopify redirects back.

sources.quote: Construct the authorization URL and redirect the merchant to it. Include a randomly generated state value (nonce) and store it so you can verify it in the next step.
const authUrl = `https:// ${ shop } /admin/oauth/authorize?` +
scope A comma-separated list of access scopes your app needs.

requests.label: Send the user to sign in

requests.text: Set expiring=1 to receive an expiring offline token and refresh token.

sources.quote: POST https://{shop}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/access_token

client_id required The client ID for the app.
client_secret required The client secret for the app.
code required The authorization code provided in the redirect.
expiring Only applies when the initial authorization request was for an offline token. Set to 1 for an expiring offline token, or 0 (default) for a non-expiring one.

requests.label: Exchange the code for tokens

requests.text: Store the newly returned access token and refresh token after every refresh.

sources.quote: POST https://{shop}.myshopify.com/admin/oauth/access_token
Every refresh returns a new access token and a new refresh token. Store both securely, and use the new refresh token in the next refresh request.

requests.label: Refresh the access token

requests.text: This makes an authenticated GraphQL Admin API request for products.

sources.quote: shopifyFetch ( `https:// ${ shop } /admin/api/2026-04/graphql.json` , {
'X-Shopify-Access-Token' : accessToken ,
body : JSON . stringify ( { query : '{ products(first: 5) { edges { node { id handle } } } }' } )

requests.label: Check the connection
requests.curl:
curl -X POST "https://YOUR_SHOP.myshopify.com/admin/api/2026-04/graphql.json" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-Shopify-Access-Token: ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  --data '{"query":"{ products(first: 5) { edges { node { id handle } } } }"}'

detail.text: Create a Shopify Partner account. Use it to create development stores and manage the public app.

sources.quote: A Shopify Partner account or a merchant store with developer permissions.

detail.text: In Partner Dashboard, register for the Shopify App Store. You need the App development and Manage financials permissions. Pay the US$19 fee, link every associated developer account, and complete identity verification before submitting a new app.

sources.quote: you need to register with the Shopify App Store for a one-time fee of $19 USD per Partner account.
During registration, you must link all of your Associated Developer Accounts to ensure revenue is tracked correctly.
Identity verification is now a required step for developers who submit new apps

detail.text: Select public distribution when creating the app. Do this carefully because Shopify does not let you change this choice later.

sources.quote: Public distribution Can be installed on multiple Shopify stores Public
You can't change the distribution method after you select it.

detail.text: Add your callback URL under [auth].redirect_urls in shopify.app.toml. Deploy the configuration before production. Shopify rejects callbacks that do not exactly match a configured redirect URL.

sources.quote: redirect_urls Yes array of string s matching a valid URL Users are redirected to these URLs as part of authorization code grant .
Instead, you can release your app configuration and extensions together with the deploy command.

detail.text: Request only the scopes needed for the first release. Put optional features in optional scopes. Request protected-customer-data access when the app needs customer data. If it needs names, addresses, phone numbers, or emails, also participate in Shopify's data-protection review.

sources.quote: Use optional scopes to offer features to some stores without requiring the same data access from every install.
Shopify will approve your app to use protected customer data if the requested data is the minimum amount required by your app to provide the merchant with the app functionality.

steps.title: Draft privacy disclosure

detail.text: Review this draft with legal counsel. Add the actual data types, AI providers, retention periods, and deletion process before publishing your privacy policy.

sources.quote: How do you use the information you collect? Do you use this information for any purposes other than providing your app's services?
For how long do you store or retain the data that you collect?

steps.output: Privacy draft: We collect only Shopify data needed to provide the requested agent feature. We use it only to operate that feature. We store data only for the stated service period. We explain retention periods and deletion options in our privacy policy. We do not use customer data for unrelated purposes.

detail.text: Create development stores in Partner tooling. Test installs and agent flows there. Do not use these stores for real transactions.

sources.quote: Dev stores are for development and testing only. They can't be used in production or process real transactions.
You don't need to submit a request for review for apps that are installed only on development stores.

detail.text: Redirect each store to its authorization URL. Exchange the returned code at that store's token endpoint. Bind state to the browser session and verify callback HMAC before storing tokens.

sources.quote: The authorization code is exchanged with a POST request using the client ID, client secret, code, and `expiring=1`.
Compare the state parameter to the nonce you stored in step 1. If they don't match, reject the request.

detail.text: Make the agent show each proposed write before saving it. Test that every write needs merchant confirmation. Keep each action narrow.

sources.quote: Ask for confirmation before writing data. Propose the change and show your UI so that the merchant can review it before anything is saved.
Keep actions small and focused.

detail.text: In Partner Dashboard, request protected-data access if the app reads customer data. Join the data-protection review if it reads names, addresses, phone numbers, or emails.

sources.quote: 1 Customer data excluding name, address, phone, and email fields Request access to protected customer data in the Partner Dashboard
2 Customer data including name, address, phone, or email fields Request access to protected customer data and fields in the Partner Dashboard
Participate in data protection reviews

steps.title: Prepare reviewer instructions

detail.text: Replace the placeholders with working access. Include every feature needed for review. Give reviewers full feature access when login is required.

sources.quote: If your app requires login credentials, you must provide valid credentials and clear, complete testing instructions that grant full feature access.

steps.output: Reviewer instructions: 1. Install the app in the supplied test store. 2. Open Agent Actions. 3. Ask for a product summary. 4. Choose a proposed product change. 5. Confirm the change in the review screen. 6. Verify the product update. Test login: [ADD TEST URL AND CREDENTIALS].

detail.text: Run the submission checks in Partner Dashboard. Add compliance webhooks, an icon, contact details, a listing, and primary language. Submit only a complete working app.

sources.quote: Apps that are distributed through the Shopify App Store must subscribe to compliance webhooks .
Every app submission must specify a primary language and create at least one Shopify App Store listing.
Submitting apps with errors, beta versions of apps, apps that don’t meet requirements, or apps with incomplete submissions can delay the process or cause your app not to be approved.

detail.text: Monitor the submission status and email. Shopify assigns a reviewer after core requirements are met. Community reports describe 5–10 business days, with longer queues possible.

sources.quote: After your app meets the core requirements, Shopify assigns a reviewer to your submission, and they begin to review your app.
It usually takes anywhere from 5-10 business days for the submission to be reviewed by our team
but this can sometimes be longer due to the time of year and how many submissions are in the queue at that time.

detail.text: Deploy the production configuration with Shopify CLI. Confirm that the deployed callback URLs and scopes match the approved app.

sources.quote: Instead, you can release your app configuration and extensions together with the deploy command.

detail.text: Preserve each raw webhook body. Verify its HMAC before reading the payload. Reject any delivery with a bad signature.

sources.quote: Always verify HMAC before trusting payload contents. Skip verification only in development with mock tools.
Reject any delivery where the signatures don't match.

gotchas.text: Do not choose custom distribution for unrelated merchants. It is limited to one store, related Plus stores, or development stores.

sources.quote: Custom distribution Installed on a single Shopify store, on multiple stores that belong to the same Plus organization, or on development stores

gotchas.text: Old orders need extra approval. read_orders covers only the latest 60 days. Older orders need read_all_orders alongside an order scope.

sources.quote: Orders are limited to the last 60 days. read_orders and write_orders cover that window.
To reach older orders, declare read_all_orders alongside either scope and follow the approval requirements for your app.

gotchas.text: Protected customer fields are redacted outside development stores until Shopify approves the app.

sources.quote: outside of dev stores the API redacts protected fields until your app meets the protected customer data requirements and is approved.

gotchas.text: An additional app cannot be listed when any existing app has fewer than ten installs on full-priced stores.

sources.quote: Each of your existing apps must have at least 10 installs on full-priced Shopify stores before you can list an additional app.

whenBlocked.text: If review feedback arrives, address it in Partner Dashboard and resubmit the corrected app.

sources.quote: After you submit your public app for review, it moves to the Submitted status and you receive an email confirming that your submission was received.

whenBlocked.text: If Partner account help is needed, contact Shopify through the Shopify Help Center.

sources.quote: For non-technical support, read our partner program documentation, or reach out to our support team on the Shopify Help Center.

whenBlocked.text: If protected-data access is denied, reduce requested fields to the minimum needed and submit a new access request.

sources.quote: Shopify will approve your app to use protected customer data if the requested data is the minimum amount required by your app to provide the merchant with the app functionality.

uncertain: Shopify provides no official numerical review service level. Community reports give 5–10 business days, but longer waits occur.
The researched sources give no timing for identity verification or protected-customer-data review.
The researched sources do not describe an appeal path for a denied protected-customer-data request.
1 claim couldn't be matched word-for-word to its cited page and is marked Unverified. Check those sources before relying on them.
